sources.design: Investigator-blinded randomised trial, n=42; bundled rehabilitation comparison.
sources.population: Sport-active adults18–60 with insertional symptoms >3 months and <3 years, VISA-A<80, running-based sport≥2/week; ultrasound-confirmed.
sources.coInterventions: Both education and progressive loading; low-compression massage/12 mm heel lifts versus high-compression stretching/end-range dorsiflexion.
sources.outcomes: VISA-A difference favored low compression:12.9 (95%CI6.2–19.6) at12 weeks;10.4 (3.7–17.1) at24 weeks. Cannot isolate range, heel lifts or omitted stretching.
sources.uncertainty: Small athletic sample; low-compression package not proof that all dorsiflexion causes injury. Supplemental brochure has stage-specific doses; symptom response does not prove tissue healing.
sources.harms: Weekly surveillance; no adverse events or discouraged cointerventions reported.
sources.limitations: Small athletic sample; low-compression package not proof that all dorsiflexion causes injury. Supplemental brochure has stage-specific doses; symptom response does not prove tissue healing. Research candidate only; no clinical release.

protocol.execution: LTCR limits dorsiflexion. Brochure p.19: long-seated straight-knee band plantarflexion, loop around forefoot, neutral to maximal plantarflexion. Page 20: same with knee slightly bent over towel. Page 21: chair-seated bilateral raise, hips/knees 90 degrees, hands at knees, neutral to maximal plantarflexion.
protocol.dose: Main text stages: isometric 5 × 30 seconds at 50% MVC to 5 × 60 seconds at 70%; isotonic 4 × 15 at 65% 1RM to 4 × 6 at 85%; energy storage 3 × 10 at 75% to 3 × 6 at 85%. Brochure p.19 band example: 8 × 15; p.20 band and p.21 chair examples: 4 × 15, 30-second rests, four seconds each direction. Preserve stage/exercise-specific differences; do not harmonise silently.
protocol.frequency: Daily rotating stages during the progressive program lasting up to twelve weeks; stage 2 alternates isometric and isotonic days. Later sport every 2–3 days. Twenty-four weeks is allocation/outcome follow-up, not the duration of weekly supervised visits.
protocol.supervision: Individual home-based and supervised progressive therapy lasted up to twelve weeks, with weekly trained physiotherapist sessions and home/gym exercise. Methods > Interventions describes this duration; Discussion says weekly supervision ended at twelve weeks. Allocation and outcome follow-up continued to twenty-four weeks, not weekly supervision.
protocol.progression: At least two weeks per stage and one week of high-load work; pain below 5/10 during, one hour after and next morning, with no weekly deterioration. Clinician decides advancement.
protocol.stoppingRules: Trial-specific monitoring in progression field; worsening prompts adjustment. Symptom response is not proof of tissue healing and is not an automatic app threshold.
